title: Explore whether investment banking is right for you
details: Learn how a bank is organized (IBD, Sales & Trading, Research) and what analysts actually do. Talk to upperclassmen who recruited for IB, and read the industry guide below.

title: Apply to freshman insight programs
details: Several banks run spring programs for first-years (for example Goldman Sachs' Possibilities Series and Citi's Freshman Discovery). Check the Programs tab for dates.

title: Confirm IB is the right path before recruiting ramps up
details: If you didn't explore IB as a freshman, do it now. Recruiting runs through sophomore fall and spring.

title: Apply to sophomore early-ID and insight programs
details: Many sophomore programs close in October and November and run over winter. They often lead to interviews or fast-tracked applications. Pin the ones you want on the Programs tab and add the deadlines to your calendar.

title: Network with upperclassmen and alumni
details: Find Vanderbilt alumni and upperclassmen in banking through LinkedIn, BBSA events, the Career Center and firm info sessions. Research each person first and lead the conversation with good questions. Send a thank-you within a day.

title: Build your behavioral and technical interview skills
details: Know the common behavioral questions cold. For technicals, cover valuation methods, DCF (WACC, CAPM, beta), EBITDA, LBO basics, enterprise vs. equity value, and how the three statements connect.

title: Keep up with markets, current events and deal flow
details: Follow the major indices, market news and recent deals at the banks you're targeting so you can discuss them in interviews.

title: Submit internship applications and attend recruiting events
details: Applications for the junior-summer internship open during sophomore year. Go to both on-campus and off-campus recruiting events, and apply early, since many banks review on a rolling basis.

title: Prepare for the interview process
details: Typical sequence: HireVue or phone screen, a first round, then a Superday of 3–5 back-to-back interviews.

title: Earn the return offer
details: Most full-time analyst offers come from the summer class. Be reliable, ask good questions and build relationships across your group.

title: Accept a return offer or recruit for full-time roles
details: If you're recruiting for full-time, reach out to your network early in the fall, since full-time spots outside the intern class are limited.

title: Protect your GPA
details: Consulting firms weigh grades heavily. Aim for about 3.8+ in A&S or Peabody, or 3.7+ in Engineering.

title: Get involved on campus and take on leadership
details: Firms look for meaningful experiences with clear personal impact, plus teamwork, leadership and initiative.

title: Attend case workshops and firm events
details: Start learning how case interviews work and meet the firms early.

title: Build experience through internships, projects or organizations
details: Anything that shows structured problem solving, quantitative work and impact.

title: Develop your "why consulting" and "why this firm" answers
details: You'll use these in networking conversations and interviews.

title: Attend info sessions and networking events
details: Build relationships, understand each firm and get noticed early.

title: Apply to first-year programs
details: Fill out the Connect with McKinsey form early (it's the way in to McKinsey's first-year summits), and look at programs like Deloitte Discovery, EY Expedition and KPMG Rise. See the Programs tab.

title: Attend info sessions and networking events
details: Build relationships, understand each firm and get noticed early.

title: Apply to sophomore early programs
details: Programs like Bain BEL, CREW and First Forward close in the fall. Pin them on the Programs tab and add the deadlines to your calendar.

title: Start case prep and get your resume and stories ready
details: Start case prepping, attend every recruiting event, and have your resume and behavioral examples ready before applications open.

title: Network heavily with consultants and recruiters
details: December through February is the key window. Attend recruiting dinners and events, and reach out to alumni at your target firms.

title: Case prep heavily and prepare behavioral examples
details: MBA case books are recommended. Practice profitability, market sizing, market entry and M&A cases with partners. CaseCoach is free through Vanderbilt.

title: Finalize your resume before spring applications open
details: Applications for the junior-summer internship have recently opened in mid-February.

title: Apply for internships
details: Deadlines have moved from summer to late winter and spring, and may keep moving earlier. Apply as soon as applications open.

title: Complete online assessments
details: McKinsey Solve, BCG Casey or Bain's online test. Invitations can come within days of applying, with short deadlines, so practice beforehand.

title: First and final round interviews
details: First round: case and behavioral interviews. Final round: more cases and behavioral questions, usually in person. The process can go from first round to offer in about a week.

title: Earn the return offer
details: Most full-time offers come from the summer intern class.

title: Take intro CS
details: Most first-year programs require at least one college CS course completed (some also want a semester of calculus).

title: Build 1–2 small projects
details: Something you can show and talk about in interviews: a website, a small app, a tool for a club.

title: Apply to first-year programs
details: Examples: Explore Microsoft, NVIDIA Ignite, SEO Tech Developer, CodePath courses. Some review applications monthly, so apply early. See the Programs tab.

title: Set up posting alerts
details: Use Simplify's internship list on GitHub and Handshake alerts so you see postings the week they open.

title: Learn data structures & algorithms
details: Practice LeetCode a few times a week, and practice explaining your approach out loud. Interviewers judge how you think as much as your answer.

title: Line up a summer internship, research or program
details: Any relevant experience the summer after sophomore year makes your junior-summer applications much stronger.

title: Build relationships that can lead to referrals
details: Most people apply with a resume and a referral. A referral helps you get the first interview.

title: Have your resume and projects ready by June
details: Junior-summer applications open in July, earlier than most other industries.

title: Junior-summer applications open: apply the first week
details: Big Tech, fintech and quant postings mostly go up July–September and review on a rolling basis.

title: Apply to junior-summer internships as postings open
details: Apply in the first week a posting opens; by October only a few big windows are still open.

title: Interview season
details: Online assessment, then 2–3 technical rounds and 1–2 behavioral rounds. Some companies now run AI-assisted coding or code-reading rounds: read every line the AI writes and test edge cases.

title: Keep applying: postings continue into spring
details: More companies keep posting from January to April, so keep checking if you're still looking.

title: Earn the return offer
details: Your junior-summer internship is the main path to a full-time offer.

title: Decide on a return offer or recruit for new-grad roles
details: New-grad postings open in late summer and fall.

title: Watch for AI lab and startup openings
details: AI labs and startups hire at any time, and their processes vary widely.

title: Build something people use
details: An app, a website, a tool for a club. Real users give you real product stories to tell.

title: Join product or startup clubs
details: Learn basic metrics and user research, and meet people who have done PM internships.

title: Aim for a tech-adjacent summer internship
details: A SWE, data or product-adjacent internship the summer after sophomore year is the usual stepping stone to a PM internship.

title: Ship a side project
details: Something you've launched and can talk about in detail: who it's for, what you decided and what you'd change.

title: Look for early-career PM tracks
details: A few companies run APM intern tracks for students earlier in school. Check the Programs tab and APMList.

title: Start practicing product-sense questions
details: "Improve X", "Design a product for Y", and metrics questions. Exponent is a good place to start.

title: Get ready for APM applications
details: Have your stories and a product portfolio ready before August, and set alerts on APMList and Simplify's APM tracker.

title: Apply to APM internships
details: Applications run August–November and some windows close within days, so apply as soon as postings open. Use referrals where you can.

title: Prepare for PM interviews
details: Product sense, metrics and experiments, and behavioral stories (STAR method). Usually a recruiter screen, a first interview, then a final round of 3–5 interviews.

title: Earn the return offer
details: Your PM internship is the main path to a full-time APM offer.

title: Apply to new-grad APM programs
details: Top programs post in early fall (often mid-September) with short windows, so track each one.

title: Read markets news daily
details: Track indices, interest rates, oil and the dollar, and be able to explain what moved and why.

title: Practice mental math
details: Quick multiplication, fractions to decimals and percentages, out loud and under a timer.

title: Apply to spring insight programs
details: Freshman programs such as Citi Freshman Discovery and Goldman Sachs' Possibilities Series open in late winter and spring. See the Programs tab.

title: Network with S&T alumni
details: Reach out to Vanderbilt alumni on trading floors through LinkedIn, BBSA events and the Career Center. Do it in the fall, before applications open.

title: Prepare a stock pitch and a trade idea
details: Have a long and a short idea ready, with the thesis and the risks for each.

title: Apply for junior-summer S&T internships
details: Most bulge brackets open in December and January. Some banks limit how many business/location combinations you can apply to, so choose carefully.

title: Interview: HireVue, then superday
details: Expect fit, markets, pitch and math questions. Practice mental math and definitions out loud with a timer, and track markets every day.

title: Prepare for the desk
details: Learn how the desks you might rotate through work (equities, rates, credit, FX, commodities), and keep following markets.

title: Summer analyst: earn the return offer
details: Learn the desks, ask questions and build relationships. Most full-time S&T offers come from the summer class.

title: Accept a return offer or recruit full-time
details: Banks hire most analysts from their intern class.

title: Prepare for quant trading interviews
details: Expect probability, brainteasers and data questions. Example: a fair coin is flipped 1,000 times (+$1 heads, −$1 tails) and you can stop any time. How do you maximize profit, and what's the chance you're ever up $3?

title: Quant trading recruiting opens
details: Quant firms recruit starting late in sophomore spring, with many technical rounds and an in-person superday.
